PART I

ITEM 1 — BUSINESS

Overview. Globex Corporation is a diversified industrial company that manufactures turbines, compressors and precision pumps for energy and aerospace customers. Our products are sold through a direct sales force and through independent distributors in more than forty countries, and a growing share of revenue comes from long-term service agreements.

Customers. Our largest customer, Initech, Inc., accounted for approximately 12% of consolidated revenue in 2025. No other customer accounted for more than 10% of revenue in any of the last three years.

Raw materials. We purchase specialty alloys, castings and electronic components from a broad base of suppliers, and we maintain safety stock for the components with the longest lead times. Backlog at year end was $21.4 billion, of which about 60% is expected to convert to revenue within twelve months.

ITEM 1A — RISK FACTORS

Our operating results depend on continued demand from the energy industry, which is cyclical and sensitive to commodity prices. A sustained decline in oil and natural gas prices would reduce our customers' capital spending and could materially reduce our revenue and margins.

Item 1A (continued)

We rely on a limited number of suppliers for specialty alloys. A disruption at any of these suppliers, including Vandelay Industries, could delay deliveries to customers and increase our costs.

Our international operations expose us to currency fluctuations, trade restrictions and changes in tax law. Roughly half of our revenue is earned outside the United States, and a stronger dollar reduces the reported value of that revenue when translated into our reporting currency.

ITEM 1B — UNRESOLVED STAFF COMMENTS

None.

ITEM 2 — PROPERTIES

We operate 14 manufacturing plants in the United States, Germany and Singapore, all of which we own, and we lease sales offices in 22 countries. We believe our facilities are adequate for our current needs and that suitable additional space will be available as required.

PART II

ITEM 7 — MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS

Revenue increased 9% to $14.2 billion in 2025, driven by double-digit growth in service agreements and the acquisition of Vandelay Industries in the second quarter. Operating margin expanded 120 basis points to 15.4%, reflecting pricing actions and productivity, partially offset by higher input costs.

Free cash flow was $2.1 billion, compared with $1.8 billion in 2024, and we returned $1.5 billion to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Segment results. Energy revenue grew 11% on higher service volumes and pricing, while Aerospace revenue grew 6% as deliveries of precision pumps recovered from the prior-year supply constraints. Corporate costs were flat, and the effective tax rate was 21.5% compared with 20.8% in 2024.
